Name: Jeconiah
Summary: Jeconiah (also called Coniah), son of Jehoiakim, reigned three months in Jerusalem before Nebuchadnezzar carried him to Babylon; after thirty-seven years in prison, Evil-merodach lifted up his head, gave him a seat above the other captive kings, and fed him at the king's table for life.
KeyStory: Jeconiah was carried to Babylon with the vessels of the Lord's house, and in the thirty-seventh year of his captivity the new king of Babylon spoke kindly to him and changed his prison garments.
RelatedPeople: Jehoiakim, King of Judah; Evil-Merodach, King of Babylon; Jeremiah; King Nebuchadnezzar; Mordecai
LifeLesson: Even a rejected king is not beyond a kindness that ends in a seat at the table.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile; Esther Saves Her People
